title: Dedalo round proposal
description: Output of `dedalo propose --json`: everything a multisig signer needs to fund one round. Dedalo signs nothing and holds no key — this is what people execute.

plan_id.description: The plan being funded. Passed on chain, so a round can be deposited once.

merkle_root.description: Root of the tree contributors prove against.

claim_program.description: Program that holds the deposit and pays claims.

token.description: Token being distributed. Null for the chain's native coin.

total.description: Sum of every claim. What the deposit must cover exactly.

instructions.description: Ordered. They are not independent: a deposit before its approval fails.

description.description: What this does, for the person deciding whether to sign.

cluster.description: Which cluster to execute on. A signer with several configured is told, not left to guess.

accounts.description: Ordered: Anchor matches them positionally, so order is part of the interface.

data.description: Instruction data, as bare hex — no `0x`. Note that `merkle_root` above IS `0x`-prefixed: a signer looking for the root inside this string has to strip the prefix first. The forms differ because `0x` is an EVM convention and Solana instruction data is not written that way; changing either now would break the contract, so the schema states it rather than hiding it.

account.description: One account the instruction takes. Exactly one of `address` and `derivation` is present: a program-derived address cannot be computed before the claim program exists, and printing a made-up one would be inventing on-chain behaviour.

derivation.description: The seeds the program must use, where the address is derived.
